title: Does Yogurt Have Less Lactose Than Milk?

seo.title: Does Yogurt Have Less Lactose Than Milk?
seo.meta_description: Yogurt often contains somewhat less lactose, and its live cultures provide lactase activity, so many people with lactose maldigestion tolerate it better than milk.
seo.search_intent: Compare lactose content and digestive tolerance of yogurt and milk.

excerpt: Yogurt often contains somewhat less lactose than milk because bacteria ferment part of the sugar, but its bigger advantage is that live cultures provide lactase activity that helps digest the remaining lactose. That is why many people tolerate yogurt better.
content_html:
A spoonful of yogurt is not simply thickened milk. During fermentation, bacteria use some lactose and also carry enzymes that help digest what remains.

The amount can be lower, but not always dramatically

Milk contains roughly 12 grams of lactose per cup. Plain yogurt can be somewhat lower, but the number varies with fermentation, concentration, and added milk solids. That is why a generic chart cannot predict every brand.

Live cultures change tolerance

Traditional yogurt cultures produce beta-galactosidase, an enzyme with lactase activity. That activity continues to help break down lactose during digestion, which explains why live-culture yogurt is often better tolerated than milk containing the same lactose dose.

Greek yogurt varies too

Straining removes whey and some lactose, but manufacturers can add milk solids or concentrates. Your actual tolerance depends on the product, serving size, and personal threshold.

faq.question: Is yogurt lactose-free?
faq.answer: No, unless it is specifically treated and labeled as lactose-free.

faq.question: Does Greek yogurt have less lactose?
faq.answer: It often does because straining removes some whey, but recipes vary.

faq.question: Why is yogurt easier to digest?
faq.answer: Live cultures provide lactase activity that helps break down lactose in the digestive tract.
